title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions it was built for, specifically as an active component in offensive cyberoperations. The Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, performed hands-on exploitation tasks, including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and authentication relay attacks, against target organizations. This is a case of a legitimate deployment being weaponized by malicious actors rather than a failure in the AI system's own logic.

The failure mode is misuse at the point of access, not a model hallucinating or a system deployed without oversight. The tool functioned largely as designed, executing commands and refining them when they failed, which is the intended behavior for an agentic coding assistant. Catching this kind of abuse would have required monitoring for anomalous usage patterns, such as commands characteristic of penetration activity rather than software development, at the platform level.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic had any awareness of this specific campaign during the period it operated, and the reporting reflects findings by security researchers, not any legal finding or confirmed attribution by a government body.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group developed a Linux ransomware variant that encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can view ransom demands. Researchers discovered the Aurora operator used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The agent performed standard hacking tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting authentication relay attacks, though many commands initially failed and required refinement.

A second Aurora cluster was identified with medium confidence, operating differently by exploiting SQL Server vulnerabilities and exfiltrating data to self-hosted storage. This cluster targeted eight organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. The investigation provided indicators of compromise including command and control IP addresses, proxy servers, file hashes, and the ransomware group's ransom negotiation website on the dark web.
